samples.summary: `--dry-run` prints the fully-built request URL to stdout with no redaction, while the same codebase deliberately strips credentials out of URLs before printing them in errors. This change widens that surface to every read command plus the api-key management routes.
samples.evidence: `printDryRunUrl` puts `url` (built by `apiV1Base`/`apiKeysUrl` from `origin(config)` = `config.server`) straight into `console.log(JSON.stringify(...))` (packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:42,48). `config.server` comes from `--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` / a YAML profile (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:90-94). The repo itself treats that value as credential-bearing: `redactUrl`'s own doc comment says "`--server`/`WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` may carry userinfo (`https://user:pass@host`) ... both would otherwise land on stderr and in CI logs" (packages/cli/src/errors.ts:86-94), and it is applied to every `fetchOrThrow` failure message (errors.ts:157,167). The dry-run printer applies no such scrubbing, so `wafflebase docs list --dry-run --server https://user:pass@host` (or the same value from `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` in CI) emits `{"url":"https://user:pass@host/api/v1/workspaces/ws-1/documents"}` on stdout — exactly the transcript an agent/CI job captures and stores. Before this change only a handful of commands reached `printDryRun`; the diff routes ~20 more commands (docs/notes/slides/files list+get, sheets tabs/cells/export) and the three `api-keys` commands through it.

samples.summary: New exported `printDryRunUrl` bypasses the dot-segment invariant `printDryRun` enforces, so any caller that builds a URL by hand can print a preview of a URL `fetch` would resolve onto a different (destructive) endpoint.
samples.evidence: `printDryRun` calls `assertNoDotSegments(path)` (dry-run.ts:28) precisely because "after encoding, no segment of `path` can be `.` or `..`, so one that is means an id reached this builder raw". `printDryRunUrl` (dry-run.ts:38) performs no such check on its `url` argument — it prints whatever string it is given. The only current caller, `previewUrl` in packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:20-22, happens to be safe because `apiKeysUrl` routes the key id through `seg()` (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:82). But the invariant is now enforced only by convention on the caller side, on the exact route where the consequence is worst: the branch's own test notes that `.../api-keys/..` resolves to `DELETE /workspaces/<ws>/`, which `@Delete('workspaces/:id')` (packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:57) serves as workspace deletion. Moving `assertNoDotSegments` into `printDryRunUrl` (where `printDryRun` would inherit it) would keep the refusal on the printing path rather than on each caller.

samples.summary: The new DNS-rebinding `Host` gate accepts a request with no `Host` header at all, so the check the docs describe as "only for a Host that is a loopback literal" is bypassable by omitting the header.
samples.evidence: `isLoopbackHost` returns `true` unconditionally when `host === undefined` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:451), and that is the value `req.headers.host` takes when a client sends no `Host` header. Node's HTTP server does not require `Host` on HTTP/1.1, so `printf 'GET /callback?code=X&state=Y HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n'` piped to the port reaches the nonce check with the loopback gate skipped entirely — the 403 at login.ts:544-547 never fires. docs/design/rest-api.md:548 and docs/design/cli.md:227-234 state the listener answers "only for a `Host` that is a loopback literal", which is not what the code enforces. Impact is bounded because the nonce (login.ts:578, constant-time at login.ts:367-376) is the real gate and a rebound *browser* always sends `Host`, so the omission only helps an attacker who could have sent `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>` anyway — but the gate is weaker than the invariant asserted for it, and it is the sole remaining request-shape check when `--allow-unbound-callback` is in use (login.ts:570-577).

samples.summary: `apiKeysUrl(config, keyId?)` silently returns the *collection* URL when `keyId` is undefined, so a per-key DELETE degrades into a collection-level DELETE instead of failing — a regression from the code it replaced.
samples.evidence: `apiKeysUrl` returns `base` (`/workspaces/<ws>/api-keys`) whenever `keyId === undefined` (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:82), and `revokeApiKey(id)` passes its argument straight through (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:416). The replaced code was `${this.apiKeysBase}/${seg(id)}`, which for a missing id produced the harmless literal `/api-keys/undefined`. Now an undefined id makes the CLI issue `DELETE /workspaces/<ws>/api-keys` — a collection-scoped destructive verb. Today that is a 404 because `ApiKeyController` declares only `@Delete(':id')` (packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.controller.ts:54) and no collection `@Delete()`, and Commander's required `<key-id>` argument makes `undefined` hard to reach from argv, hence medium confidence. The same shape applies to the `--dry-run` preview (packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:82). Making the id a required parameter of a separate builder (or throwing on `undefined`) removes the footgun.

samples.summary: `workspaceSeg`'s empty-workspace exemption rests on "`/workspaces//documents` matches no route at all", which stops holding behind a reverse proxy that merges duplicate slashes (nginx `merge_slashes` is on by default).
samples.evidence: `workspaceSeg` deliberately emits an empty segment for an unconfigured workspace (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:64-66), and the doc comment justifies it with "every path built on it has further segments (`/documents`, `/api-keys`), so `/workspaces//documents` matches no route at all". That reasoning is about Express routing only. A fronting proxy that collapses `//` (nginx's default `merge_slashes on`) rewrites `GET /workspaces//api-keys` to `GET /workspaces/api-keys`, which matches `@Get('workspaces/:id')` (packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:39) with `:id` = the literal `api-keys`; `WorkspaceService.resolveId` resolves non-UUID values as a **slug** (packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.service.ts:209-221), so a workspace slugged `api-keys` (or `documents`, `files`) would be addressed instead of the request erroring. `assertMember`/`assertOwner` still run, so this is a wrong-target rather than an authorization bypass, and it needs both a slash-merging proxy and a colliding slug — hence low confidence. Refusing an empty workspace at request-build time (with a "no workspace selected" message) rather than emitting an empty segment would remove the dependency on downstream path normalisation.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. printDryRunUrl (packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:38-49) serializes the url argument straight into console.log(JSON.stringify(...)) with no scrubbing; its only guard is assertNoDotSegments (dry-run.ts:52-60), which addresses path traversal, not credentials. The URL is built by apiV1Base/apiKeysUrl from origin(config) = config.server verbatim (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:43-45,69-71,80-83), and config.server is taken unvalidated from --server / WAFFLEBASE_SERVER / session / YAML profile (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:90-94,116-119,137-141,155-158). The repo itself classifies that exact value as credential-bearing: redactUrl's doc names --server/WAFFLEBASE_SERVER userinfo (https://user:pass@host) and strips userinfo plus query/hash (packages/cli/src/errors.ts:86-112), and it is applied to every transport failure message (errors.ts:157,167) and throughout docs/image-fetcher.ts. A grep of all ~25 printDryRun/printDryRunUrl call sites (docs.ts:87,116,133,152,173,207,262; notes.ts; slides.ts; files.ts; cells.ts; tabs.ts; sheets-export.ts:57; sheets-import.ts:114; api-keys.ts:42,61,82) shows no caller applies redactUrl, so nothing upstream or downstream makes this unreachable. This is sensitive-data / credential exposure to stdout - squarely in the Security lens's secrets lane - and blocking at major severity since it is a clear weakness rather than a self-contained exploit.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The "finding" is the review harness's own failure message, not a claim about repository code: scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637 constructs exactly the quoted string in poolExhaustedError() with kind "pool-exhausted", meaning the reviewer agent could not open an SDK session because every OAuth credential slot in the process pool was retired. No file, line, or code path is alleged to be vulnerable. The condition is a documented CI capacity/infra event (docs/tasks/active/20260820-fixer-live-credential-todo.md:1-34, 106-123; scripts/agent/pick-fix-credential.mjs:1-34), whose remaining action is manual secret registration. It is also not a secrets-exposure issue: the message interpolates only pool.size, and the pool's diagnostics are names-only by construction (scripts/agent/token-pool.mjs:155-157, 184-187 map slot.name, never slot.token). Nothing here touches authorization, injection, crypto/signature verification, SSRF, deserialization, or path traversal, so it is outside the Security lens and not a blocking code defect.
